how: A member asks the room to work toward putting its icon on the canvas.
The opening proposal specifies the icon as the mark the room could make.
The success assessment supplies a completion-state report without identifying the builders or their pixel contributions.
The invitation supplies an anchor coordinate through its canvas link even though the earlier search found no coordinate vocabulary.
The completion report does not describe upkeep and cannot establish whether it occurred.
The celebration supplies no account of damage or of identifying who changed the work.
The invitation and celebration leave restraint toward neighbouring works unobserved.
The shared-build invitation does not expose border negotiations or treaties.
The invitation to make a logo does not expose an attack on another work.
The linked location does not recount a lost spot or a move.

The immediate success report and celebration do not expose further recording of the work's fate.
The final celebration does not expose a decision about carrying the effort forward.
